name: Vivid lilac
lede: Vivid Lilac is a saturated light purple recorded only in the 2010 xkcd color survey, where our library files the name itself with the older spelling Liliac.

sections.title: A vivid build on lilac
sections.body: The nearest named colors on file are [[baby-purple]], [[bright-lilac]], [[floral-lavender]] and [[floral-lavender]], at 3.9, 5.6, 6.2 and 6.2 ΔE [2]. Our own library entry for this exact swatch spells the name Liliac rather than Lilac, an older or variant spelling carried over from that survey [2]. The ISCC-NBS system classes the hue as brilliant purple, about 6.7 units from that block's center [1]. Its Munsell notation is 3.2P 6.7/14.4 and its LCH values are lightness 68, chroma 63, hue 311 degrees [1]. In sRGB its components run 196 red, 142 green and 253 blue, with blue leading and red a clear second, the pattern of a purple pulled toward pink rather than blue [1]. See [[lilac]] for the paler flower color this name intensifies.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within CIEDE2000 4 of Vivid Lilac covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole: a purple this saturated is rare in aged, varnished oil paint [3].
